_about: Authored words for the matrices page of the endpoint card. A block is keyed by the questions it holds (the clustering decides those, m1-cluster.js); if the blocks change, gen-matrices.js stops and asks for names. Plain lines follow gabe-lens plain mode and are checked by ../workflow-panel/plain-audit.py. Numbers are never typed here: {tokens} are filled by the generator.

Q1+Q2+Q9.name: Data effects
Q1+Q2+Q9.plain: The rows the endpoint touches, the moment it touches them, and the fate of each change.
Q1+Q2+Q9.standpoint: Your first standpoint: what we read, write, modify, create and delete.

Q3+Q11.name: Endings
Q3+Q11.plain: The ways a request can end, and the expected one among them.
Q3+Q11.standpoint: The destinations in your standpoint on what determines the path. The forks that lead to them sit in Gates and decisions.

Q4.name: Proof
Q4.plain: The conditions a test proves, and the ones nothing reaches.
Q4.standpoint: Your coverage standpoint, the part the lab calls Tests.

Q5+Q7.name: Stages and order
Q5+Q7.plain: The stations a request passes, and the order in which things run.
Q5+Q7.standpoint: Your stage spine, read as a sequence. It is the time axis of the console.

Q6+Q17.name: Gates and decisions
Q6+Q17.plain: The checks that stop a request and the forks that decide its ending.
Q6+Q17.standpoint: Your standpoint on what determines the path. The part the lab calls Security lands here, because a gate is one kind of fork.

Q10+Q13.name: Structures
Q10+Q13.plain: The shapes of the body that comes in and the body that goes out.

Q15+Q18+Q19.name: Functions
Q15+Q18+Q19.plain: The code that runs, sorted by how much it decides.
Q15+Q18+Q19.standpoint: Your functions standpoint, from the one facing the API down to the little helpers.

Q16.name: In-flight state
Q16.plain: The values that stay alive only while the request runs.
Q16.standpoint: Your standpoint on what is saved temporarily and alive during the process. The map cannot read most of it yet.

Q14+Q20.name: Overview and risk
Q14+Q20.plain: The whole endpoint at a glance, and the things about it that look wrong.
Q14+Q20.standpoint: None of your standpoints names it. It is what the face and the command panel answer before any view is chosen.

Q12.name: Standard or specialist
Q12.plain: The pieces this endpoint is built from, set against the pieces most endpoints share.
Q12.standpoint: None of your standpoints names it. It is the common versus specialist lens from your forward ideas, and it compares endpoints instead of reading one.

Q8.name: Client
Q8.plain: The screen's side of each ending.
Q8.standpoint: Your reach outward standpoint, the one the lab calls widening.

levels.name: far
levels.plain: The face of the card, as it sits on the graph or in a list.

levels.name: mid
levels.plain: The open card in the middle panel, under one point of view.

levels.name: near
levels.plain: One part of the open card, drilled into.

levels.name: portrait
levels.plain: The full record of the one thing you clicked.

forms.mark: A single mark or label — present or absent, one value.
forms.count: A number, with no names yet.
forms.chips: A short row of named pieces.
forms.list: The full list, with the specifics of each item.
forms.full: The complete record, nothing held back.
forms.alert: An alert — invisible at rest, drawn on the face only when the value is abnormal.

m1: A filled block means its questions lean on the same attributes, so one point of view can answer them together.
A square outside every block is an attribute one view borrows from another.
The raters are three agents, not people. Each judged from a different seat: the operator at the console, the data engineer, and the minimalist.

The three marked {cells} cells between them, and {filled} stay filled after the merge. All three agreed on {unanimous}, and were one step apart on {adjacent}. On {split} one said needed and another said not needed, and a fourth agent ruled as judge.
prisms: All six parts of the lab come back as blocks: data, schemas as structures, functions, tests as proof, security as gates and decisions, and widening as the client.
Five more blocks stand beside them: the endings, the stages and their order, in-flight state, the overview, and the comparison of one endpoint against the rest.
{nSingle} blocks hold a single question. Nothing joined them, which is weak evidence for a view of their own.
The cut falls at the widest gap in the joins, between {simAbove} and {simBelow}. The joins just past it are your merge candidates. {weak}.
spine: “{top}” is needed most. {topNeed} of {nq} questions cannot be answered without it.
The top of this list is the face of the card. Everything lower appears only inside its own view.
A rating of 3 does not earn the face by itself. {n3} attributes are rated 3, and the face holds about {budget}.
m2: Read a row left to right. The first mark is where the attribute first shows.
The words earlier and later mark where the questions moved an attribute away from my first guess in the inventory.
A bell at the far view is an alert. It stays invisible until the value is abnormal.
left: A question listed here needs an attribute the inventory lacks, or one the map cannot produce yet.
An attribute no question needs is a candidate to cut, or a sign that one of your questions is still missing.

unanswered.title: Gaps the raters named
unanswered.plain: A question where two or more raters said the inventory lacks something.

unneeded.title: Attributes no question needs
unneeded.plain: An attribute that only ever helps, and never decides an answer.
unneeded.none: Every attribute is needed by at least one question.

blocked.title: Needed, but the map cannot produce it yet
blocked.plain: An attribute a question needs that waits on new generation work.
blocked.none: Nothing that is needed waits on the map.

keep.plain: A point of view worth its own entry in the command panel.

merge.plain: A block that belongs inside another point of view — name that view in the note.

drop.plain: A block that is no point of view at all.

ownWord.plain: The share of these attributes' use that falls inside this view — a short bar means the view mostly borrows.

ladderWord.plain: The similarity at which two groups of questions would join — a long bar means they lean on the same attributes.

cutWord.plain: The cut — the widest drop between two joins in a row, so everything above it joined and nothing below it did.
